versions.provenance: 8th edition urothelial (bladder) carcinoma TNM, rewritten in original wording from criteria published on public references (cancer.org and standard 8th edition bladder staging) after the Medscape article returned a paywall; invasion criteria, node criteria, and stage mappings preserved exactly. versions.introduction:
The 8th edition staging system applies to urothelial (bladder) carcinoma. The pivotal distinction is between non-muscle-invasive disease (Ta, Tis, T1) and muscle-invasive disease (T2 and higher). The T category tracks progressive invasion from the urothelial lining (Ta/Tis) through the lamina propria (T1), the inner and outer muscularis propria (T2a/T2b), perivesical fat (T3a microscopic, T3b macroscopic), and adjacent organs or the pelvic/abdominal wall (T4a/T4b).

Nodal disease is graded by the number and location of involved nodes: true-pelvis nodes are N1 (single) or N2 (multiple), common iliac nodes are N3, and M1 is split into distant nodal (M1a) and non-nodal (M1b) metastasis. 8th edition retained this framework from the 7th Edition; the main practical nuance is that any node above the aortic bifurcation is distant (M1a) rather than regional.

t.label: Urothelial carcinoma in situ: flat, non-invasive high-grade tumor confined to the urothelium
Tumor invades the subepithelial connective tissue (lamina propria)
Tumor invades the muscularis propria (detrusor muscle)
Tumor invades the superficial (inner half of the) muscularis propria
Tumor invades the deep (outer half of the) muscularis propria
Tumor invades perivesical soft tissue microscopically
Tumor invades perivesical soft tissue macroscopically (extravesical mass)
Tumor invades any of: prostatic stroma, seminal vesicles, uterus, vagina, pelvic wall, or abdominal wall
Tumor invades the prostatic stroma, seminal vesicles, uterus, or vagina
Tumor invades the pelvic wall or abdominal wall

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
Metastasis in a single regional node in the true pelvis (perivesical, obturator, internal or external iliac, or sacral node)
Metastasis in multiple regional nodes in the true pelvis (perivesical, obturator, internal or external iliac, or sacral nodes)
Metastasis in a common iliac lymph node or nodes

m.label: Distant metastasis limited to lymph nodes beyond the common iliac nodes
Non-lymph-node distant metastasis (for example bone, liver, lung)

stageGroups.basis: Single true-pelvis node with T1 to T4a primary.
Multiple true-pelvis nodes or common iliac nodes with T1 to T4a primary.
Invasion of pelvic or abdominal wall.
Distant nodal metastasis beyond the common iliac nodes.

versions.regionalNodes: Regional nodes are the true-pelvis nodes: perivesical, obturator, internal iliac (hypogastric), external iliac, and presacral/sacral nodes, along with the common iliac nodes. Single true-pelvis node involvement is N1, multiple true-pelvis nodes is N2, and common iliac node involvement is N3. Nodes above the aortic bifurcation are distant metastasis (M1a).
versions.histologicGrade: Urothelial carcinoma is graded as low-grade or high-grade under the WHO 2004/2016 two-tier system (the older WHO 1973 grade 1 to 3 scheme may still be reported). Carcinoma in situ (Tis) is by definition high-grade.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Most bladder cancers are urothelial (transitional cell) carcinomas. Recognized aggressive variants include micropapillary, nested, plasmacytoid, sarcomatoid, and urothelial carcinoma with squamous or glandular differentiation. Pure squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, and small cell (neuroendocrine) carcinoma also occur and carry distinct prognoses.
prognosticFactors: Depth of invasion, especially non-muscle-invasive (Ta/Tis/T1) vs muscle-invasive (T2 and higher)
Presence of concurrent carcinoma in situ
Regional node status and location (true pelvis vs common iliac)
Response to intravesical therapy in non-muscle-invasive disease
